mainTopic: Habits of תפילה and respect for the בית הכנסת, and a chain of sayings from רבי חלבו in the name of רב הונא
overview: The amud opens with the last line about the תפילין of הקדוש ברוך הוא: all the פסוקים are written together in the arm-תפילין. Then come many teachings about תפילה and the בית הכנסת. When a regular misses בית הכנסת for ordinary business, ה׳ asks about him, because he should have trusted in ה׳. ה׳ is angry when there are not ten men in the בית הכנסת. A person should keep a fixed place for תפילה like אברהם, should not rush out of the בית הכנסת, and should run in and run to learn, even on שבת. A list of sayings follows about the 'main reward' of different מצוות: running, crowding, reasoning, silence, צדקה, crying at a הספד, and words at a wedding. רב הונא calls one who prays behind the בית הכנסת facing away a רשע, and a story about אליהו shows how serious this is, followed by explanations of 'כרם זלות לבני אדם'. The amud ends with more sayings of רבי חלבו in the name of רב הונא: be careful with מנחה (others add ערבית and שחרית), make a חתן happy, a God-fearing person is listened to, and greet others first and always return a greeting.

steps.title: Closing the earlier discussion: all the verses are in the arm-תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The last line of the earlier discussion: in the arm-תפילין of הקדוש ברוך הוא, all the פסוקים are written together.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all of them are written together in His arm-תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the earlier discussion about the תפילין of הקדוש ברוך הוא. It says that in the arm-תפילין, all the פסוקים are written together in one place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, the גמרא said the head-תפילין have four separate compartments, each holding its own פסוקים. This line adds the contrast: the arm-תפילין have only one compartment, so everything sits together. With this, that topic is closed.

keyTerms.meaning: all of them (the פסוקים in the תפילין)

steps.confusionAlert: This line belongs to the topic before it, not to the teaching about בית הכנסת that comes next. Do not try to connect it to רבי יצחק's statement.

phrases.english: And all of them are written on His arm.
phrases.notes: 'His arm' means the arm-תפילין of הקדוש ברוך הוא from the earlier discussion, which have only one compartment.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכוּלְּהוּ כְּתִיבִי בְּאֶדְרָעֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the earlier sugya on the תפילין of הקדוש ברוך הוא, which began before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In the arm-תפילין of הקדוש ברוך הוא, all the פסוקים are written together in one compartment.

steps.title: When a regular misses בית הכנסת, God asks about him
steps.stepSummary: רבין בר רב אדא quotes רבי יצחק: if someone who always comes to בית הכנסת misses one day, הקדוש ברוך הוא asks about him. The proof is a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין בר רב אדא said in the name of רבי יצחק: Whoever usually comes to בית הכנסת and one day does not come, הקדוש ברוך הוא asks about him. As the פסוק says: 'Who among you fears ה׳, listens to the voice of His servant, and walked in darkness and has no light?'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רבי יצחק says that God notices when a regular member of the בית הכנסת is missing and asks about him, and he brings a פסוק as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק opens with a question, 'Who among you…?' That is God asking about someone. It describes a person who fears ה׳ and should have been listening to 'the voice of His servant,' meaning the prayers. Instead he 'walked in darkness,' leaving early in the morning before תפילה. So the question in the פסוק is God asking where this regular person went.

keyTerms.meaning: one who is used to doing something regularly
asks about him, inquires after him

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that keeping a steady habit of coming to בית הכנסת matters to הקדוש ברוך הוא, so that even one missed day is noticed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבִין בַּר רַב אַדָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Ravin bar Rav Adda said that Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Anyone who is used to coming to the synagogue
and one day did not come,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, asks about him,
as it says: 'Who among you fears the Lord,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 50:10

phrases.english: who listens to the voice of His servant,

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר הָלַךְ חֲשֵׁכִים וְאֵין נֹגַהּ לוֹ״.
phrases.english: who walked in darkness and has no light?'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִין בַּר רַב אַדָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: כׇּל הָרָגִיל לָבֹא לְבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching. It is not connected to the תפילין discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a regular attendee of בית הכנסת misses a day, הקדוש ברוך הוא asks about him (based on ישעיהו 50:10).

steps.title: It depends on why he was absent: מצוה or ordinary business
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the words 'has no light': if he went for a מצוה, he does have light; if he went for ordinary business (דבר הרשות), he has no light.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he went for a מצוה, there is light for him. But if he went for an ordinary matter, there is no light for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the end of the פסוק, 'and has no light,' by splitting it into two cases based on why the person missed בית הכנסת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'no light' does not apply to everyone who was absent. A person who left to do a מצוה is protected by that מצוה, so he does have light. Only a person who left for his own ordinary affairs is the one the פסוק describes as having no light.

keyTerms.meaning: a matter of a מצוה, a religious duty
an optional, ordinary matter, such as business

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as saying everyone who misses בית הכנסת is punished. The 'no light' is only for someone who left for ordinary business, not for a מצוה.

phrases.aramaic: אִם לִדְבַר מִצְוָה הָלַךְ — נוֹגַהּ לוֹ,
phrases.english: If he went for a matter of a מצוה, there is light for him,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לִדְבַר הָרְשׁוּת הָלַךְ — אֵין נוֹגַהּ לוֹ.
phrases.english: but if he went for an optional matter, there is no light for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם לִדְבַר מִצְוָה הָלַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the last words of the פסוק quoted in step 2 and limits them to someone who was absent for ordinary business.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone absent for a מצוה has 'light.' Only someone absent for a דבר הרשות 'has no light.'

steps.title: Why does the verse say 'let him trust in ה׳'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next words of the פסוק, 'let him trust in the name of ה׳,' and asks what the reason behind them is.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Let him trust in the name of ה׳.' What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the next words of the same פסוק. It is setting up the answer that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having said that the person who left for business 'has no light,' the גמרא wants to know why he is treated so strictly. The פסוק's next words, 'let him trust in the name of ה׳,' hint at the reason, so the גמרא asks what they are teaching.

phrases.english: 'Let him trust in the name of the Lord.' What is the reason?
phrases.notes: These are the next words of the same פסוק in ישעיהו.

steps.triggerLanguage: יִבְטַח בְּשֵׁם ה׳ מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues with the rest of the פסוק and asks why the person who left for ordinary business gets 'no light.'
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the reason behind the words 'let him trust in the name of ה׳,' and why is this person treated so strictly?

steps.title: Because he should have trusted in ה׳ and did not
steps.stepSummary: The answer: he should have trusted in ה׳ that he would lose nothing by praying first, and he did not trust.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he should have trusted in the name of ה׳, and he did not trust.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The person is judged strictly because he did not trust ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He skipped תפילה because he was worried about his business. He should have trusted that ה׳ would take care of him even if he went to pray first. His lack of trust is why he 'has no light.'
steps.whatToRemember: A regular attendee of בית הכנסת who misses a day is noticed by הקדוש ברוך הוא. If he left for a מצוה, he has light. If he left for business, he has no light, because he should have trusted in ה׳ and prayed first.

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ לִבְטוֹחַ בְּשֵׁם ה׳,
phrases.english: Because he should have trusted in the name of the Lord,
and he did not trust.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ לִבְטוֹחַ בְּשֵׁם ה׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He is judged strictly because he should have trusted in ה׳, coming to תפילה first without fear of loss, and he did not.

steps.title: ה׳ is angry when there are not ten men in בית הכנסת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that when הקדוש ברוך הוא comes into a בית הכנסת and does not find ten men there, He becomes angry right away, as the פסוק in ישעיהו says.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: When הקדוש ברוך הוא comes into a בית הכנסת and does not find ten men there, He becomes angry right away. As the פסוק says: 'Why did I come and there is no man? I called and no one answers.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבי יוחנן on the same theme of coming to בית הכנסת: ה׳ wants to find ten men there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier teaching (step 2) was about one regular person who misses a day. Now the focus is on the whole group: if there is no group of ten, ה׳ is angry. The פסוק fits well: 'I came' means ה׳ comes to the בית הכנסת, and 'no one answers' means there is no group of ten to answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Ten men, the number needed for a group prayer
As it says (introducing a פסוק as proof)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בָּא בְּבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת,
phrases.english: When the Holy One, Blessed be He, comes into a synagogue,
and does not find ten men there,
He becomes angry right away,
as it says: 'Why did I come and there is no man,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 50:2

phrases.english: I called and no one answers?'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בָּא בְּבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new, related teaching about coming to בית הכנסת, moving from the single regular person to the group of ten.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When ה׳ comes to a בית הכנסת and does not find ten men, He becomes angry immediately.

steps.title: A fixed place for תפילה brings the help of the God of אברהם
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלבו, quoting רב הונא, teaches that whoever sets a fixed place for his תפילה has the God of אברהם helping him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חלבו said in the name of רב הונא: Whoever sets a fixed place for his תפילה, the God of אברהם is his help.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching about regular תפילה: having one set place to pray earns the help of the God of אברהם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a new idea: not only coming to pray regularly, but praying in the same place each time. The phrase 'God of אברהם' hints that this habit comes from אברהם, which the גמרא will prove in steps 9 and 10.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sets a fixed place

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chelbo said in the name of Rav Huna:
Whoever sets a fixed place for his prayer,
the God of Avraham is his help.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: כׇּל הַקּוֹבֵעַ מָקוֹם לִתְפִלָּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching on the same broad theme of steady, regular תפילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who sets a fixed place for his תפילה is helped by the God of אברהם.

steps.title: He is eulogized as a student of אברהם
steps.stepSummary: The same teaching continues: when such a person dies, people mourn him by calling him humble and pious, one of the students of אברהם אבינו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when he dies, people say about him: 'Where is the humble one? Where is the pious one? He was one of the students of אברהם אבינו!'
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching of רב הונא continues and describes how the person with a fixed place for תפילה is praised at his death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Setting a fixed place for תפילה makes him a 'student' of אברהם, because אברהם did the same. So he is remembered with אברהם's good traits, being humble and pious.

keyTerms.meaning: Pious person, one who does more than the minimum

phrases.english: And when he dies, they say about him:
'Where is the humble one, where is the pious one,
one of the students of Avraham our father!'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֶׁמֵּת, אוֹמְרִים לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same statement of רב הונא, adding the praise given at the person's death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who fixes a place for תפילה is eulogized as humble, pious, and a student of אברהם אבינו.

steps.title: How do we know אברהם had a fixed place?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that אברהם אבינו set a fixed place for his תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אברהם אבינו, from where do we know that he set a fixed place?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for something the teaching assumed: that אברהם had a fixed place for תפילה. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 7 and 8 called this person a student of אברהם because of his fixed place. That only works if אברהם himself had a fixed place, so the גמרא wants a פסוק to show it.

phrases.english: And Avraham our father, from where do we know
that he set a fixed place?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ מְנָא לַן דִּקְבַע מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the assumption in steps 7 and 8 that אברהם had a fixed place.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that אברהם אבינו had a fixed place for תפילה.

steps.title: Proof from the פסוק: אברהם returned to the place where he 'stood'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves it from בראשית: אברהם got up early to 'the place where he had stood.' And 'standing' means praying, as we see from פינחס, who 'stood and prayed.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And אברהם got up early in the morning to the place where he had stood.' And 'standing' always means תפילה, as it says: 'And פינחס stood and prayed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with two פסוקים: one shows אברהם returned to the same place, and the other shows that 'standing' means praying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק by itself only says אברהם went back to where he had 'stood.' The second פסוק, about פינחס, shows that 'standing' in a פסוק can mean praying. Put together: אברהם went back to the same place where he had prayed, so he had a fixed place for תפילה.
steps.whatToRemember: Having a fixed place for תפילה is a habit learned from אברהם אבינו, who went back to the same place where he had 'stood,' and 'standing' means praying.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the well-known practice of having a מקום קבוע, a set place, for one's תפילה.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And Avraham got up early in the morning
to the place where he had stood,'
phrases.notes: בראשית 19:27

phrases.english: and 'standing' means nothing other than prayer,
as it says: 'And Pinchas stood and prayed.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 106:30

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיַּשְׁכֵּם אַבְרָהָם בַּבֹּקֶר אֶל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר עָמַד שָׁם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 9 with a פסוק and a supporting definition.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אברהם went back to 'the place where he had stood,' and 'standing' means praying (from פינחס), so he had a fixed place for תפילה.

steps.title: Do not take big steps when leaving the synagogue
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלבו, quoting רב הונא, teaches that one who leaves the בית הכנסת should not take a large stride.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חלבו said in the name of רב הונא: A person leaving the synagogue should not walk out with big steps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching from רבי חלבו in the name of רב הונא: don't hurry out of the בית הכנסת with big steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Big, fast steps on the way out look like the person is eager to get away from the בית הכנסת. This is a new rule about showing respect to the place of תפילה, in the same series as the earlier teachings of רב הונא.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chelbo said, Rav Huna said:
One who leaves the synagogue
should not take a large stride.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same speakers as Step 7; a new teaching about respect for the בית הכנסת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When leaving the בית הכנסת, one should not take large strides.

steps.title: אביי: the rule is only for leaving, but running in is a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: אביי limits רב הונא's rule to leaving. When going in to the בית הכנסת, it is a מצוה to run, based on a פסוק in הושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This rule was only said about going out. But going in, it is a מצוה to run, as the verse says: 'Let us run to know God.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains how far רב הונא's rule goes: it only covers leaving. Going in, you should actually run.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same action, rushing, means opposite things depending on the direction. Rushing out shows you want to leave; rushing in shows you are eager to come close to ה׳. The פסוק 'נרדפה לדעת את ה׳' backs up the idea of running toward Him.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this about… (a phrase that limits a rule)

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not arguing with רב הונא. He agrees, and is just explaining that the rule against big steps applies only on the way out.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לָא אֲמַרַן, אֶלָּא לְמִיפַּק.
phrases.english: Abaye said: We only said this for going out.
But for going in,
it is a מצוה to run,
as it is said: "Let us eagerly pursue knowing God."
phrases.notes: הושע 6:3

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לָא אֲמַרַן, אֶלָּא לְמִיפַּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule of Step 11 to leaving and adds the opposite rule for entering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on big strides is only for leaving; entering the בית הכנסת, it is a מצוה to run.

steps.title: רבי זירא at first thought running to the lecture on שבת was wrong
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says that at first, seeing the רבנן run to the lecture on שבת, he thought they were desecrating שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: At first, when I saw the רבנן running to the lecture on שבת, I said: 'The רבנן are desecrating שבת.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא begins a personal story about running on שבת. This step sets up the problem; the next step tells what changed his mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Running on שבת is normally not proper for the holiness of the day, so רבי זירא was bothered. The question is whether running to learn תורה is different, which the next step answers.

keyTerms.meaning: The public lecture given by a rabbi

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: At first,
when I would see the Rabbis
running to the lecture on Shabbat,
I would say: "The Rabbis are desecrating Shabbat."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: מֵרֵישׁ כִּי הֲוָה חֲזֵינָא לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of running for holy purposes (Step 12), now raising the problem of running on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי זירא first assumed running on שבת, even to a lecture, was a desecration of שבת.

steps.title: A teaching that one should run to learn הלכה even on שבת
steps.stepSummary: After hearing רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching (through רבי תנחום) that one should always run to a matter of הלכה, even on שבת, רבי זירא started running too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once I heard what רבי תנחום said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: 'A person should always run to a matter of הלכה, even on שבת, as the verse says: They shall go after God, He will roar like a lion,' I too run.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא tells what changed his mind: a teaching that running to learn הלכה is right even on שבת. So now he runs too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general concern about running on שבת does not apply when running to learn תורה. The פסוק compares following ה׳ to responding to a lion's roar: you rush. This settles the problem from Step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: He will roar like a lion

steps.whatToRemember: Running into the בית הכנסת shows eagerness and is a מצוה, and one should run to learn הלכה even on שבת. Only rushing *out* is improper.

phrases.english: Once I heard this teaching

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי תַּנְחוּם אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: of Rabbi Tanchum, who said in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
A person should always run to a matter of halacha
and even on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אַחֲרֵי ה׳ יֵלְכוּ כְּאַרְיֵה יִשְׁאָג״ וְגוֹ׳,
phrases.english: as it is said: "They shall go after God, He will roar like a lion," etc.,
phrases.notes: הושע 11:10

phrases.english: I too run.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דִּשְׁמַעְנָא לְהָא דְּרַבִּי תַּנְחוּם אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves רבי זירא's concern from Step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That running to learn תורה is proper even on שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע בן לוי (via רבי תנחום), based on הושע 11:10.

steps.title: The reward for the lecture is for the running
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says the main reward for going to the lecture is for running to get there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: The reward for the lecture is the running.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא adds a short saying: what earns reward at the lecture is mainly the eagerness of running to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many listeners may not fully understand the lecture, but they still earn reward for their effort and eagerness. This ties back to the theme of running to learn from Step 14.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
The reward for the lecture is the running.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: אַגְרָא דְפִרְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on running to the lecture by stating the reward for it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The main reward for attending the lecture is for the effort of running to it.

steps.title: The reward for the כלה gathering is for the crowding
steps.stepSummary: אביי, in the same style, says the main reward for attending the כלה gathering is for putting up with the crowding.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The reward for the כלה is the crowding.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a matching saying: at the big כלה gathering, the reward is mainly for squeezing in through the crowd.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבי זירא's saying, this teaches that reward comes from the effort and discomfort of coming to learn, not only from how much one understood. The two sayings are built in the same pattern.
steps.whatToRemember: Reward for Torah learning comes largely from the effort: running to the lecture and pushing through the crowd.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The reward for the kalla is the crowding.
phrases.notes: Here כלה means the big public learning gathering, not a bride.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אַגְרָא דְכַלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel saying to Step 15, in the same pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The main reward for attending the כלה is for enduring the crowding.

steps.title: The reward for learning is for the reasoning
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the main reward for learning שמועות is for the logical thinking that goes into them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The reward for learning traditions is for the reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds another line to the list. He says that when you learn, the main reward comes from working out the logic, not just from knowing the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same model as steps 15 and 16: a מצוה has one main part that earns the reward. Here the main part of learning is the סברא, meaning the effort to understand why the הלכה is what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: A learned tradition or teaching, especially a הלכה

phrases.english: Rava said:
The reward for learning traditions is for the reasoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַגְרָא דִשְׁמַעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new item to the 'main reward' series started by רבי זירא and continued by אביי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The main reward for learning comes from the reasoning, not only from knowing the conclusions.

steps.title: The reward for visiting mourners is for the silence
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the main reward for going to a house of mourning is for sitting quietly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The reward for going to a house of mourning is for the silence.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds the next item. When you visit mourners, the main reward comes from being quiet with them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the מצוה is comforting mourners. According to רב פפא, its most valuable part is not talking a lot but sitting in silence.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
The reward for going to a house of mourning is for the silence.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַגְרָא דְבֵי טַמְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same 'main reward' pattern and applies it to visiting mourners.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The main reward for visiting a house of mourning comes from the silence.

steps.title: The reward for fasting is for the charity
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא says the main reward for a fast day is for the צדקה given on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: The reward for fasting is for the charity.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא adds another item. On a fast day, the main reward comes from the צדקה that is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not eating is not the most important part of a תענית. According to מר זוטרא, the main reward comes from helping the poor that day.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
The reward for fasting is for the charity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַגְרָא דְתַעֲנִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same 'main reward' pattern and applies it to a fast day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The main reward for a fast day comes from the charity given on it.

steps.title: The reward for a eulogy is for making people cry out
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the main reward for a הספד is for getting the listeners to raise their voices and cry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: The reward for a eulogy is for raising the voice.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת adds another item to the list. When giving a הספד, the main reward comes from moving people to cry out in grief.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A good הספד is not just a speech. Its goal is to make people feel the loss, and that emotional result is what earns the main reward.

keyTerms.meaning: Raising up the voice in crying

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
The reward for a eulogy is for raising the voice.
phrases.notes: Literally 'lifting up': getting the listeners to raise their voices and cry.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַגְרָא דְהֶסְפֵּדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same 'main reward' pattern and applies it to a eulogy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The main reward for a eulogy comes from moving the listeners to cry out.

steps.title: The main reward for a wedding is for the words
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the main reward for attending a wedding is for the good words said to the חתן and כלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The main reward for going to a wedding is for the words.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds the last item to the list of 'main reward' statements. He says the main reward for a wedding comes from the words spoken there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the earlier statements, this one points to the real heart of a מצוה. At a wedding, simply showing up is not the main thing. The main reward comes from gladdening the חתן and כלה with warm words and blessings.

keyTerms.meaning: Words, here meaning the good wishes said at a wedding

steps.whatToRemember: The 'main reward' series (steps 15–21: רבי זירא, אביי, רבא, רב פפא, מר זוטרא, רב ששת, רב אשי) teaches that every מצוה has a central element where most of its value lies. Those elements are running to the lecture, crowding at the כלה, reasoning in learning, silence with mourners, צדקה on a fast day, moving people in a הספד, and words of joy at a wedding.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The reward for a wedding is for the words.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַגְרָא דְבֵי הִלּוּלֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Last entry in the parallel list of 'main reward' sayings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The main reward for attending a wedding is for the words that bring joy to the couple.

steps.title: Praying behind the synagogue makes one called wicked
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that someone who prays behind the בית הכנסת is called a רשע, based on a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Anyone who prays behind the בית הכנסת is called 'wicked,' as it says: 'The wicked walk round about.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the topic of respect for the בית הכנסת. רב הונא says that praying behind the building earns someone the name רשע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone inside faces one direction. Someone praying behind the building may end up facing the opposite way, which looks like he is turning his back on the בית הכנסת. The פסוק 'סביב רשעים יתהלכון' is read as describing people who circle around to the back.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Anyone who prays behind the synagogue
is called "wicked,"
as it says: "The wicked walk round about."
phrases.notes: תהלים 12:9

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַמִּתְפַּלֵּל אֲחוֹרֵי בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת נִקְרָא רָשָׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the 'main reward' list and returns to the theme of honoring the בית הכנסת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Praying behind the בית הכנסת earns the label רשע, learned from 'סביב רשעים יתהלכון'.

steps.title: The rule applies only when not facing the synagogue
steps.stepSummary: אביי limits רב הונא's rule. It only applies when the person does not turn his face toward the בית הכנסת.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We only said this when he does not turn his face toward the בית הכנסת. But if he does turn his face toward the בית הכנסת, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי narrows רב הונא's statement. Standing behind the building is fine as long as the person faces toward it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not where the person stands. It is that he turns his back on the בית הכנסת. If he stands behind it but faces it, he is facing the same way as the people inside, so there is no disrespect.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this in the case of..., a phrase that limits a rule
We have no problem with it

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not arguing with רב הונא. He is explaining exactly when רב הונא's rule applies.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
We only said this
where he does not turn his face toward the synagogue,
but if he turns his face toward the synagogue,
we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא מַהְדַּר אַפֵּיהּ לְבֵי כְּנִישְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the exact case that רב הונא's rule covers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Praying behind the בית הכנסת is only a problem when one faces away from it. Facing toward it is permitted.

steps.title: אליהו kills a man praying with his back to the synagogue
steps.stepSummary: A story shows how serious the matter is. A man prayed behind the בית הכנסת without facing it, and אליהו, disguised as an Arab, rebuked him and killed him.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man was praying behind the בית הכנסת and did not turn his face toward it. אליהו passed by and saw him. אליהו appeared to him as an Arab traveler and said to him: 'Is this how you stand before your Master?!' He drew a sword and killed him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about exactly the case אביי described: praying behind the building while facing away. The harsh ending shows how serious this is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man fits אביי's case exactly, because the story stresses that he did not face the בית הכנסת. אליהו's rebuke, 'Is this how you stand before your Master?', shows the real problem: תפילה is standing before the Master, and turning one's back is disrespect.
steps.whatToRemember: Facing away from the בית הכנסת while praying behind it is treated as real disrespect to the Master you are standing before.

phrases.english: A certain man was praying
behind the synagogue,
and did not turn his face toward the synagogue.
Elijah passed by.
He saw him, and appeared to him as an Arab traveler,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כְּדוּ בָר קָיְימַתְּ קַמֵּי מָרָךְ?!
phrases.english: He said to him: Is this how you stand before your Master?!
phrases.notes: "Your Master" means הקב"ה, whom you stand before in תפילה.

phrases.english: He drew a sword and killed him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא גַבְרָא דְּקָא מְצַלֵּי אֲחוֹרֵי בֵּי כְּנִישְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the forbidden case defined by אביי and shows how serious it is.
steps.raayaObject: The seriousness of praying behind the בית הכנסת while facing away from it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story in which אליהו punishes a man who did exactly this.

steps.title: What does the end of the פסוק mean?
steps.stepSummary: A חכם asks רב ביבי בר אביי (or רב ביבי asks רב נחמן בר יצחק) what the words "כרם זלות לבני אדם" mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the Sages said to רב ביבי בר אביי (some say רב ביבי said to רב נחמן בר יצחק): What do the words "כרם זלות לבני אדם" mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move. It asks what the second half of the same פסוק means, the פסוק רב הונא used about praying behind the בית הכנסת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא used only the first half of the פסוק, "סביב רשעים יתהלכון." Now the גמרא wants to understand the rest of it. There are two versions of who asked whom, and the question itself is the same in both.

keyTerms.meaning: One of the Sages, a חכם who is not named

phrases.english: One of the Sages said
to Rav Beivai bar Abaye,
and some say Rav Beivai said
to Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak:
What is the meaning of "When vileness is exalted among the sons of men"?
phrases.notes: תהלים 12:9, the end of the same פסוק רב הונא used about the רשע.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״כְּרֻם זֻלּוּת לִבְנֵי אָדָם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the story about אליהו to explain the rest of רב הונא's פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the words "כרם זלות לבני אדם".

steps.title: Very important things that people treat lightly
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the פסוק is talking about matters that stand at the very top of the world, yet people treat them as cheap.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: These are things that stand at the height of the world, and people treat them lightly.
steps.whatsHappening: The question is answered. The פסוק describes people who treat lightly things that are truly lofty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads "כרם" as "height" and "זלות" as "treating something lightly." Together the words mean that something high and lofty is treated as cheap by people. This fits the topic: someone who disrespects תפילה is treating a lofty thing as cheap.

keyTerms.meaning: The height of the world, matters of the greatest importance

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ דְּבָרִים שֶׁעוֹמְדִים בְּרוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם,
phrases.english: These are things that stand at the height of the world,
phrases.notes: He reads the word כְּרֻם as coming from רוּם, "height."

phrases.english: and people treat them lightly.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵלּוּ דְּבָרִים שֶׁעוֹמְדִים בְּרוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק refers to lofty matters that people treat as unimportant.

steps.title: Needing other people makes a person's face change
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר read the same words differently: when a person has to depend on others, his face changes color like a כרום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר both said: Once a person comes to need other people, his face changes like a כרום, as it says: "Like a כרום is the lowliness of people."
steps.whatsHappening: Two great אמוראים give a different explanation of the same words in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here "כרם" is not "height." It is the name of something whose color changes. "זלות" is the shame a person feels when he must depend on others. So the פסוק says that a person who has fallen to needing others changes color like a כרום.

keyTerms.meaning: Came to need other people, depending on them for help

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the same reading as step 26. There, כרם meant "height." Here, כרום is the name of something that changes colors, which step 29 will explain.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar
both said:
Once a person comes to need other people,
his face changes like a kerum,
as it is said:
"Like a kerum is the lowliness of people."
phrases.notes: Same words as before, but now read as "like a כרום" instead of "when it is high."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר דְאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second reading of the same words explained in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who must depend on others is shamed, and his face changes color like a כרום.

steps.title: What is a כרום?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the כרום mentioned by רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a "כרום"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move. It asks what the word כרום means in רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר's comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison in step 27 only works if we know what a כרום is and how it changes. The question asks for that missing piece.

keyTerms.meaning: The thing the face is compared to, still unexplained here

phrases.english: What is a "kerum"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״כְּרוּם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a word used in step 27.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word כרום.

steps.title: The כרום is a bird that changes colors
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי explains that the כרום is a bird in the coastal cities that turns many colors when the sun shines on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: There is a bird in the cities by the sea called כרום, and when the sun shines it turns many colors.
steps.whatsHappening: The question is answered. רב דימי tells us that a כרום is a bird whose colors keep changing in the sunlight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the comparison is clear. Just as this bird changes color when the sun shines on it, a person who must depend on others changes color from embarrassment. This finishes the explanation of the פסוק according to רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: When רב דימי came (to בבל from ארץ ישראל)

steps.whatToRemember: The words "כרם זלות לבני אדם" get two readings. (1) People treat lofty things such as תפילה lightly. (2) Someone who depends on others is shamed and changes color like the כרום bird.

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
There is a certain bird in the cities by the sea,
and its name is "kerum,"
and when the sun shines
it turns into several colors.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אָמַר: עוֹף אֶחָד יֵשׁ בִּכְרַכֵּי הַיָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28 and completes the comparison of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כרום is a coastal bird that changes many colors in the sunlight.

steps.title: Depending on others is like being punished by fire and water
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי and רבי אסי say that a person who needs other people is like someone punished with two punishments, fire and water, based on a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי and רבי אסי both said: it is as if he were judged with two punishments, fire and water, as the פסוק says: 'You let men ride over our heads; we went through fire and water.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is one more view on the person who has to depend on others, continuing right after רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר's comparison to the כרום bird. רבי אמי and רבי אסי say it is as bad as fire and water together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק joins 'men riding over our heads', meaning being under other people's control, with 'fire and water'. So רבי אמי and רבי אסי read being under others' control as a double punishment. This raises the level beyond רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר, who only said a person's face changes color.

keyTerms.meaning: You let men ride over our heads, meaning You put us under other people's control

steps.whatToRemember: Needing other people is described as painful: the face changes like a כרום, and it is like being punished by fire and water.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי דְאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi, who both said:
It is as if he were judged with two punishments,
fire and water, as it is said:
"You caused men to ride over our heads;
phrases.notes: תהלים 66:12

phrases.english: we went through fire and water."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי דְאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another opinion on depending on others, after the explanation of the כרום bird
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Depending on others is like being punished with both fire and water.

steps.title: Be extra careful with the afternoon prayer
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says a person should always be careful with תפילת המנחה, because אליהו was answered in that prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חלבו said in the name of רב הונא: a person should always be careful with תפילת המנחה, because אליהו was answered only at מנחה, as the פסוק says: 'And it was at the time of the מנחה offering, and אליהו the prophet came near and said... Answer me, ה׳, answer me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching from רבי חלבו in the name of רב הונא: take extra care with מנחה. The proof is that אליהו's prayer on הר הכרמל was answered at that time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the time was 'בעלות המנחה', when the afternoon offering was brought in the בית המקדש. Since such a famous prayer was answered at that hour, רב הונא learns that מנחה is a special time for prayer. The 'ו' at the start of 'ואמר' shows this is another teaching from רבי חלבו, who was quoted earlier on the דף.

keyTerms.meaning: At the time the afternoon offering was brought
Short for 'and so on', meaning the פסוק continues

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known source for why מנחה gets special attention.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Chelbo said in the name of Rav Huna:
A person should always be careful
with the afternoon prayer,
for Eliyahu was not answered
except in the afternoon prayer,
as it is said: "And it was at the time of the afternoon offering,
phrases.notes: מלכים א 18:36. This is the showdown on הר הכרמל.

phrases.english: that Eliyahu the prophet came near and said, etc.:
Answer me, ה׳, answer me."
phrases.notes: מלכים א 18:37

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: לְעוֹלָם יְהֵא אָדָם זָהִיר בִּתְפִלַּת הַמִּנְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new topic: special care for the times of prayer
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should always be careful with מנחה, because אליהו was answered at that time.

steps.title: Why אליהו said 'answer me' twice
steps.stepSummary: The first 'ענני' asked for fire to come down from heaven. The second asked that the people should not say it was sorcery.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Answer me': that fire should come down from heaven. 'And answer me': that they should not say it is an act of sorcery.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to explain the double 'ענני' in the פסוק it just quoted. Each 'answer me' was a different request.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק repeats 'ענני', and the גמרא reads each one as a different request. First אליהו asked for the miracle itself. Then he asked that the people would not say the fire was magic.

keyTerms.meaning: An act of sorcery or magic

phrases.english: "Answer me": that fire should come down from heaven,
and "answer me": that they should not say
that it is an act of sorcery.
phrases.notes: 'They' means the people watching, who might think the fire was magic and not from ה׳.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״עֲנֵנִי״ — שֶׁתֵּרֵד אֵשׁ מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side explanation of the פסוק quoted in the previous step
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each 'ענני' was a separate request: one for the fire, and one so the people would not think it was sorcery.

steps.title: Be careful with the evening prayer too
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן adds that a person should also be careful with תפילת ערבית, based on 'מנחת ערב' in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: also with the evening prayer, as the פסוק says: 'Let my prayer be set as incense before You, the lifting of my hands as the evening offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds ערבית to רב הונא's rule. He says a person should be careful with that prayer too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק compares prayer to the 'evening offering', so דוד המלך's own prayer was connected to the evening. The word 'אף', meaning 'also', shows רבי יוחנן agrees about מנחה and adds ערבית to it.

keyTerms.meaning: Incense offered in the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'מנחה' in 'מנחת ערב' means an offering. It is not the afternoon prayer we call מנחה.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אַף בִּתְפִלַּת עַרְבִית,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: Also with the evening prayer,
as it is said: "Let my prayer be set as incense before You,
phrases.notes: תהלים 141:2

phrases.english: the lifting of my hands as the evening offering."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אַף בִּתְפִלַּת עַרְבִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens רב הונא's rule to include ערבית
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should also be careful with ערבית.

steps.title: Be careful with the morning prayer too
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק adds that a person should also be careful with תפילת שחרית, based on 'בקר' in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: also the morning prayer, as the פסוק says: 'ה׳, in the morning You will hear my voice; in the morning I will arrange my prayer to You and wait.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק adds שחרית, so all three daily prayers now get special care. This ends the section on being careful with prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'בקר' twice. This shows that דוד המלך made a point of praying in the morning and hoped to be answered then. So שחרית also deserves special care.

keyTerms.meaning: I will arrange, set out my prayer

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: be careful with מנחה, because of אליהו. רבי יוחנן adds ערבית. רב נחמן בר יצחק adds שחרית. Each one brings his own פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: אַף תְּפִלַּת שַׁחֲרִית,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: Also the morning prayer,
as it is said: "ה׳, in the morning You will hear my voice;
phrases.notes: תהלים 5:4

phrases.english: in the morning I will arrange my prayer to You and wait."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: אַף תְּפִלַּת שַׁחֲרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds שחרית after רבי יוחנן added ערבית
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should also be careful with שחרית.

steps.title: Enjoying a wedding meal without making the groom happy
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלבו quotes רב הונא: whoever benefits from a חתן's meal but does not make him happy goes against the five voices in ירמיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חלבו said in the name of רב הונא: Anyone who enjoys the meal of a חתן and does not make him happy goes against the five voices, as the פסוק says: 'The voice of joy and the voice of gladness, the voice of the groom and the voice of the bride, the voice of those who say: Give thanks to ה׳ צבאות.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רב הונא: a guest who eats at a wedding has to help make the חתן happy. If he doesn't, he goes against five 'voices' listed in a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ירמיהו lists five 'קול' phrases tied to a wedding. רב הונא uses that count of five to show how serious it is to eat at a wedding without adding joy. This number five will become the basis for the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: The wedding meal of a groom

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Ḥelbo said that Rav Huna said:
Anyone who benefits from the feast of a groom
and does not make him happy
goes against the five voices,
phrases.notes: Literally 'passes over five voices.' He means this person goes against the five 'קול' phrases in the פסוק that follows.

phrases.english: as it says: 'The voice of joy and the voice of gladness,
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 33:11

phrases.english: the voice of the groom and the voice of the bride,

phrases.aramaic: קוֹל אוֹמְרִים הוֹדוּ אֶת ה׳ צְבָאוֹת״.
phrases.english: the voice of those who say: Give thanks to the Lord of hosts.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching in the same chain of sayings from רב הונא (via רבי חלבו), moving from תפילה to the joy of a wedding.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever enjoys a חתן's meal without making him happy goes against the five voices of ירמיהו 33:11.

steps.title: What is the reward for making the groom happy?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the other side: if someone does make the חתן happy, what is his reward?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he does make him happy, what is his reward?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the positive side of the last teaching. This short question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 35 told us what goes wrong when you don't make the חתן happy. Now the גמרא wants to know the good result when you do. The answer will also connect to the number five.

phrases.english: And if he does make him happy, what is his reward?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם מְשַׂמְּחוֹ מַה שְּׂכָרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Flips the previous teaching to ask about the reward for doing the right thing.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What reward a person receives for making the חתן happy.

steps.title: He merits the תורה, given with five voices
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי answers: he merits the תורה, which was given with five voices, as seen in the פסוקים about הר סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: He merits the תורה, which was given with five voices, as it says: 'And it was on the third day, when it was morning, there were voices and lightning and a heavy cloud on the mountain, and the voice of a שופר... And the voice of the שופר... and God answered him with a voice.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי answers the question: the one who makes the חתן happy merits the תורה. He shows from the פסוקים that the תורה was given with five voices.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The five voices of the wedding match the five voices of מתן תורה. The count is: 'קולות' (plural, so two), the first שופר, the second שופר, and the voice God answered with, making five. The reward matches the act: five voices of joy lead to the תורה of five voices.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
He merits the Torah
which was given with five voices,
as it says: 'And it was on the third day, when it was morning,
phrases.notes: שמות 19:16

phrases.english: there were voices and lightning,
phrases.notes: 'קולות' is plural, so it counts as at least two voices.

phrases.english: and a heavy cloud on the mountain,
and the voice of a shofar, etc.
And the voice of the shofar, etc.
phrases.notes: שמות 19:19. This is a second mention of the שופר, so it counts as another voice.

phrases.english: and God answered him with a voice.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: זוֹכֶה לַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 36.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He merits the תורה, which was given with five voices (two from 'קולות', two שופר mentions, and God's answering voice).
steps.whyThisMatters: It links a wedding to מתן תורה through the matching number five, showing how much weight חז״ל give to making a חתן happy.

steps.title: Another verse mentions more voices at סיני
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the count of five: another פסוק says the whole nation 'saw the voices,' which seems to add more.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But it is written: 'And the whole nation saw the voices!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהושע בן לוי's count of five voices. Another פסוק about הר סיני mentions more 'voices', so it looks like there were more than five.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תורה was given with exactly five voices, the extra 'קולות' in this פסוק would push the number past five. That would break the match with the five voices of the wedding.

phrases.english: Is that so? But it is written:
'And the whole nation saw the voices!'
phrases.notes: שמות 20:15

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִּי? וְהָא כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the count of five voices from step 37.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן לוי's claim that the תורה was given with five voices.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another פסוק mentions additional 'קולות' at הר סיני, so the total seems to be more than five.

steps.title: Those voices came before the giving of the תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: the voices in that פסוק happened before מתן תורה, so they are not counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those voices were before the giving of the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The voices in the other פסוק came before the actual moment the תורה was given, so they don't count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only voices at the moment of giving the תורה are part of the count of five. The extra voices the nation saw were earlier, so the number five stays.
steps.whatToRemember: Making a חתן happy is tied to the five voices of a wedding, and its reward is the תורה, given with five voices. Voices before מתן תורה are not part of that count.

phrases.english: Those voices
were before the giving of the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹתָן קוֹלוֹת, דְּקוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה הֲווֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 38.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Timing distinction: the extra voices happened at a different time.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All voices mentioned at הר סיני count, making more than five.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the voices at the moment of מתן תורה count; the extra ones came earlier, so the count stays at five.

steps.title: Making a groom happy is like bringing a thanks-offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו gives another answer about the reward for making a חתן happy: it is as if he brought a קרבן תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: It is as if he offered a thanks-offering, as the verse says: 'Those who bring a thanks-offering to the house of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the question from step 36 in a different way. He says making a חתן happy is like bringing a קרבן תודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי said the reward is getting the תורה. רבי אבהו reads further in the same פסוק in ירמיהו, which also talks about the joy of a חתן and כלה. Right after that, the פסוק mentions people bringing a תודה, so he links the two.

keyTerms.meaning: A thanks-offering brought in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
It is as if he offered a thanks-offering,
as it is stated: 'Those who bring a thanks-offering to the house of ה׳.'
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 33:11. This is the same פסוק that has the five voices.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר: כְּאִילּוּ הִקְרִיב תּוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side issue about counting the voices, the גמרא goes back to the question in step 36 and gives a different answer from the one in step 37.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the reward of one who makes a חתן happy?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is as if he brought a קרבן תודה, as the same פסוק mentions people bringing a תודה.

steps.title: Making a groom happy is like rebuilding a ruin of ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a third answer: it is as if he rebuilt one of the ruins of ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It is as if he rebuilt one of the ruins of ירושלים, as the verse says: 'For I will bring back the captivity of the land as at the beginning, says ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives one more answer to the same question. He says making a חתן happy is like rebuilding part of ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses the end of the same פסוק in ירמיהו, which talks about ה׳ bringing the land back to how it was before. So all three answers come from one פסוק, and each person focuses on a different part of it.

keyTerms.meaning: Captivity, the exiled state that ה׳ will reverse
As at the beginning, as it was before

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
It is as if he rebuilt one of the ruins of Jerusalem,
as it is stated: 'For I will bring back the captivity of the land
as at the beginning, says ה׳.'
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 33:11. These are the closing words of the same פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: כְּאִילּוּ בָּנָה אַחַת מֵחוּרְבוֹת יְרוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is another answer to the same question, built on the last words of the פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the reward of one who makes a חתן happy?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is as if he rebuilt one of the ruins of ירושלים.

steps.title: A person who fears Heaven is listened to
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלבו quotes רב הונא: anyone who has יראת שמים, people listen to his words. The source is a פסוק in קהלת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חלבו said in the name of רב הונא: Any person who has fear of Heaven, his words are listened to, as the verse says: 'The end of the matter, all is heard: fear God,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from the same pair of רבי חלבו and רב הונא. It says that when someone truly fears ה׳, people listen to what he says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof reads the words 'all is heard' together with 'fear God.' It understands the פסוק to mean that everything a God-fearing person says will be heard. This opens a new topic that is not about the חתן.

keyTerms.meaning: Fear of Heaven, awe of ה׳
Short for וגומר: 'and so on,' meaning the פסוק continues

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Chelbo said that Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם —
phrases.english: Any person who has fear of Heaven in him,
his words are listened to,
as it is stated: 'The end of the matter, all is heard:
fear God,' and so on.
phrases.notes: קהלת 12:13. The rest of the פסוק is 'and keep His commandments, for this is all of man,' which the גמרא asks about next.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This starts a new topic, connected to the earlier steps only because it comes from the same רבי חלבו and רב הונא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who has יראת שמים is listened to, based on קהלת 12:13.

steps.title: What does 'for this is all of man' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the end of the פסוק in קהלת means: 'for this is all of man.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'for this is all of man'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the end of the פסוק it just quoted. This question sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording 'this is all of man' is unclear. How can one God-fearing person be 'all' of mankind? The גמרא wants an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: What is, what does it mean
All of man, the whole of mankind

phrases.english: What is meant by 'for this is all of man'?
phrases.notes: These are the last words of קהלת 12:13, the part covered by the 'and so on.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״כִּי זֶה כׇּל הָאָדָם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא asks for an explanation of the end of the פסוק quoted in step 42.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the phrase 'כי זה כל האדם.'

steps.title: The whole world was created for this person
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers: הקדוש ברוך הוא said the whole world was created only for the sake of this God-fearing person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said: The entire world was created only for the sake of this one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר explains the phrase. A person who fears ה׳ is the reason the world was created.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'this is all of man' to mean that this person is what all of creation is for. The word 'this' points to the God-fearing person.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
The entire world was not created
except for the sake of this one.
phrases.notes: 'This one' means the person who fears ה׳ and keeps His מצוות.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the question in step 43.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The whole world was created only for the God-fearing person.

steps.title: This person is worth as much as the whole world
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר כהנא explains it differently: the God-fearing person is equal in value to the whole world.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר כהנא said: This one is equal to the entire world.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא בר כהנא gives a second explanation of 'this is all of man.' He says this one person is as weighty as the whole world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר said the world exists for this person. רבי אבא בר כהנא says something a little different: this person and the whole world are equal in worth, like two sides of a scale.

keyTerms.meaning: Equal in weight, equal in value

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁקוּל זֶה כְּנֶגֶד כׇּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ,
phrases.english: This one is equal to the entire world.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר כָּהֲנָא אָמַר: שָׁקוּל זֶה כְּנֶגֶד כׇּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a second answer to the question in step 43, different from רבי אלעזר's answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The God-fearing person is equal in value to the whole world.

steps.title: The whole world was created to keep this person company
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן עזאי, or some say רבי שמעון בן זומא, says the whole world was created to be company for the God-fearing person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן עזאי says, and some say רבי שמעון בן זומא says: The entire world was created only to be company for this one.
steps.whatsHappening: A third explanation of 'this is all of man' is given. Some say it is from בן עזאי and some say it is from בן זומא. It says the rest of the world was made to be company for the God-fearing person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes even further than the earlier answers. The rest of the world is described as the companions of the God-fearing person, so that he will not be alone. The גמרא is not sure who said it, so it gives both names.

keyTerms.meaning: To be company for, to keep someone company

steps.whatToRemember: The phrase 'כי זה כל האדם' gets three explanations of how great a God-fearing person is: the world was created for him (רבי אלעזר), he is equal to the whole world (רבי אבא בר כהנא), or the world was created to keep him company (בן עזאי or בן זומא).

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Azzai says,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן זוֹמָא אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Shimon ben Zoma says:
The entire world was not created
except to be company for this one.
phrases.notes: לצוות comes from צוותא, 'company.' The rest of the world is here so this person is not alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן עַזַּאי אוֹמֵר, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן זוֹמָא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the third answer to the question in step 43, and it ends this short section.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The whole world was created to be company for the God-fearing person.

steps.title: Greet first someone who usually greets you
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלבו quotes רב הונא: if you know someone usually greets you, you should greet him first, based on the פסוק "seek peace and pursue it."
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חלבו said in the name of רב הונא: anyone who knows that his friend usually greets him should greet that friend first, as the פסוק says: "Seek peace and pursue it."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching from the same pair, רבי חלבו quoting רב הונא. This one is about saying שלום to people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Answering a greeting is not enough here. If you already know this person will greet you, you should beat him to it and say שלום first. The proof is the word "pursue" in the פסוק: you do not just accept peace when it comes, you go after it.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace. Here it means a greeting, like saying hello
Used to, in the habit of
He should go first, do it before the other person

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Chelbo said, Rav Huna said:
Anyone who knows about his fellow
that he is used to greeting him,
should greet him first,
as it is stated: "Seek peace and pursue it."
phrases.notes: תהלים 34:15

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching from the same pair as step 42, on a new topic: greetings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If you know someone usually greets you, you should greet him first, because the פסוק says to pursue peace.

steps.title: Someone who doesn't return a greeting is called a robber
steps.stepSummary: The second half of רב הונא's teaching: if someone greets you and you do not answer, you are called a גזלן, based on a פסוק in ישעיהו about the stolen goods of the poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if his friend greeted him and he did not answer, he is called a "robber," as the פסוק says: "And you have eaten up the vineyard; the spoils of the poor are in your houses."
steps.whatsHappening: This continues the same teaching. Now it covers the opposite case, where someone ignores a greeting that was already given to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 47 was about going above the minimum by greeting first. This step is about the minimum itself: answering a greeting is owed, so ignoring it is like taking something that belongs to the other person. The פסוק talks about stealing from a poor person, who may own nothing except his greeting, so refusing to answer him is a kind of theft.

keyTerms.meaning: Returned. Here it means answered the greeting
A robber, someone who takes what belongs to another
What was robbed from the poor person

steps.whatToRemember: Two levels of greeting: if you know someone usually greets you, greet him first (pursuing peace). If someone greets you, you must answer, and ignoring him makes you a גזלן.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think "robber" here means taking money. The text calls him a גזלן for ignoring a greeting, because answering it is something the other person is owed.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that answering a greeting is an obligation between people, not just good manners.

phrases.english: And if he greeted him and he did not return it
he is called a "robber,"
as it is stated: "And you have eaten up the vineyard;
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 3:14

phrases.english: the spoils of the poor are in your houses."
phrases.notes: A poor person may have nothing to take except his greeting, so ignoring it is stealing from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם נָתַן לוֹ וְלֹא הֶחֱזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same teaching of רב הונא, moving from the extra step of greeting first to the basic duty of answering a greeting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who does not return a greeting is called a גזלן, as shown from the פסוק about the spoils of the poor.
